why: Cross-type rule (operator, 2026-09-26; compare-spec 2.16.0): an Episode classed Pilot is a candidate for a Basic record and is compared under its SERIES' title -- a pilot sold or listed as a TV movie carries the show's name, while the registry record for the episode is titled 'Pilot'. Scored on the Basic profile and capped into Review. The Series' title is on a record that is neither the submission nor the candidate (Episode -> Season -> Series), so it arrives through the `ancestry` block (specs/golden-pairs.md section 2; De-Dupe UI S-32). Pins that the comparison happens under the Series' title: title quality reaches 0.95 and the pair reaches Review; an implementation that cannot climb compares 'Pilot' against 'Night Train' and FAILS loudly. S-32 described this fixture as a pilot with only a SYSTEM title; on the registry such titles are '<Series>: Season 1: Episode 1' (sampled 2026-10-13), which already contain the Series' title, so the climb decides nothing there and a fixture of that shape would pass without the block. The user-titled 'Pilot' is the shape the climb exists for, and a common one
